body:
Follow-up from the capability taxonomy v0 investigation (#2027, record: `doc/2026-10-29T14-05-00Z_investigation_capability_taxonomy/`, PR #2337).

## Goal
Specify **and** prototype the MQTT device bridge (`id.device.v1`) — the recommended ESP32 path: ID speaks MQTT directly, so devices get the same wants/result/refusal semantics as web instead of terminating at Home Assistant.

## Why this path
Taxonomy §5 compares (a) firmware → MQTT → Home Assistant, (b) ID speaks MQTT directly, (c) direct web, and recommends (b) as the device path with (a) as interop and (c) unchanged: only (b) keeps one capability model and one refusal vocabulary at the last hop.

## Scope
- Topic schema: `<prefix>/manifest` (retained, on connect), `<prefix>/wants`, `<prefix>/cap/result`, `<prefix>/surface`, `<prefix>/events`; one connection per device, per-world prefix.
- Wire bounds identical to WebSocket: 64 KiB frames, 8 KiB args; a 128×64 1-bit screen is ~1 KiB of cells, which is why pixel screens are the existing `Screen` variant at smaller dimensions rather than a new kind.
- Rotary encoders as `Key` events with a signed delta in `args`.
- Minimum `time.tick` interval for the device path to avoid wake storms.
- **Decisions:** retained `wants` (recommend: manifest only, wants never retained — a retained wants replays a stale request); TLS/auth; reconnect/backoff; journaling on the device side.
- Firmware implements only `device.info`, small `screen`/`text`, a closed `form.*` subset, `loc.position` when GNSS is present, and key/encoder events.

## Acceptance
- A written schema doc with example documents for each topic.
- A PoC **clearly labelled as a PoC** (the issue's rule: never build the permanent feature on an unreviewed PoC) — a host-side bridge plus a fake device that connects, publishes a manifest, receives a wants document and gets a `cap: result`, in an integration test.
- Home Assistant interop recorded as out-of-scope-but-supported.

## Out of scope
Firmware for a specific board, OTA, ESPHome components, power profiling.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written id.device.v1 schema doc exists with example documents for each topic (manifest retained on connect; wants; cap/result; surface; events) and the wire bounds identical to WebSocket (64 KiB frames, 8 KiB args)
- [ ] The open decisions are recorded with recommendations: retained wants (recommend manifest only — a retained wants replays a stale request), TLS/auth, reconnect/backoff, device-side journaling, minimum time.tick interval
- [ ] A PoC — clearly labelled as a PoC, never the permanent feature — host-side bridge plus a fake device connects, publishes its manifest, and answers a want with result/refusal semantics matching web
- [ ] Firmware scope stays the closed subset: device.info, small screen/text, closed form.* subset, loc.position when GNSS present, key/encoder events (rotary encoder as Key with signed delta)



---

## Triage verdict — 2026-11-08 (queue task 12058)

**Verdict: REAL AND CURRENT.** This is the full verdict; the comment POST is blocked by GitHub's secondary content-creation rate limit, so it is carried in the issue body until that clears.

### Fresh evidence (`00ca4186`, 2026-11-08T18:10Z)
- #2343 is OPEN; no hard-stop labels.
- PR search for `id.device.v1` returns only merged PR #2337 — the capability-taxonomy investigation, not an implementation. No schema examples, wire code or PoC.
- `git grep -i mqtt -- pkgs/id/src` returns no matches.
- #5901 is CLOSED with the constrained-device decision: retained manifest only, TLS plus per-device credentials, the closed device subset, and bridge-as-translator. It names #2343 as the bridge implementation follow-up, so those are inputs here, not open questions.
- #2028 keeps production hardware rollout deferred; #5783 owns boards, firmware, OTA and power and is out of scope.

### Live remainder, scoped into the follow-up packet
1. `id.device.v1` schema with example documents for manifest, wants, cap/result, surface and events; per-world prefix, one connection per device, 64 KiB frame / 8 KiB args bounds.
2. Recommendations for reconnect/backoff, device-side journaling and minimum `time.tick`, reusing #5901's decisions without reopening them.
3. A clearly labelled non-production host bridge plus fake-device integration PoC proving manifest publication, wants/result/refusal semantics, stale retained-wants rejection, bounds enforcement and fail-closed authentication.

### Routing
- Fix packet **task 13917** queued on `repo-health-code-pilot`, dedupe key `repo-health:v1:fix:developing-today/code:issue:2343`.
- #2343 stays OPEN and closes only through a merged PR, never through this triage.
